findings.message: Domain Model Distortion — Edits bypass the activity log. Symptom: `ActivityEntry.action` includes `'updated'`, and `addItem` and `deleteItem` both add activity entries. `updateItem` (`src/hooks/useInventory.ts:43`) only changes the item. This PR is the first to put `updateItem` in front of users (`App.tsx:27`, `InventoryPage.tsx:121`). Source: Evans — Domain-Driven Design, Ubiquitous Language. The model says "updated" is an activity, but the code never records one. Consequence: A user can change an item's quantity or price and nothing appears in the Dashboard activity feed. The feed then gives a wrong history, and the low-stock count can change with no recorded cause. Remedy: Add an `'updated'` activity entry in `updateItem`, built the same way as in `deleteItem`. The timestamp-formatting block is already copied in two places, so pull it into a `createActivity(action, itemName, details)` helper first rather than adding a third copy.

Cognitive Overload — `AddItemModal` now runs two modes from optional props, and one path fails silently. Symptom: `AddItemModal.tsx:38` checks `isEditMode && editItem && onUpdate` and otherwise calls `onAdd(form)`. Both `editItem` and `onUpdate` are optional. The component is still called `AddItemModal` even though it also edits. Source: Fowler — Refactoring, Flag Arguments. `editItem` works as a hidden mode switch that splits the component into two behaviors. Consequence: If a future caller passes `editItem` but leaves out `onUpdate`, saving creates a duplicate item instead of an error. The compiler won't flag it, and the name misleads readers about what the component does. Remedy: Rename it to `ItemFormModal`. Model the props as a discriminated union, for example `{ mode: 'add'; onAdd } | { mode: 'edit'; item; onUpdate }`, so TypeScript rejects edit mode without an update handler.

Coverage Illusion — The new edit and reset behavior is untested. Symptom: The commit adds edit-mode prefill, the Edit button, the "Save Changes" path and form reset on close. The only new test covers delete activity logging, which this diff doesn't change. Source: Feathers — Working Effectively with Legacy Code, Ch. 1 Consequence: The bugs most likely to come back are not caught by any test: a stale form after closing, edit calling `onAdd`, or prefill missing a field. Remedy: Add React Testing Library tests for `InventoryPage`: - Clicking "Edit X" prefills the form, and saving calls `onUpdate(id, …)` but not `onAdd`. - Opening, typing, closing and opening "Add" again shows an empty form.

Accidental Complexity — A key counter forces the modal to remount, and the modal depends on the caller doing it. Symptom: `InventoryPage` uses three state variables to drive the modal (`isModalOpen`, `editingItem`, `modalKey`). The comment in `AddItemModal.tsx:24` says its form only resets correctly because the parent bumps `key`. Source: Ousterhout — A Philosophy of Software Design, Ch. 5: Information Leakage Consequence: The modal works correctly only if the parent does this. Any other parent that reuses it without the key trick brings back the stale-form bug. Remedy: Render it conditionally with `{isModalOpen && <ItemFormModal … />}`. That remounts the modal on every open, so you can delete `modalKey`, the `isOpen` prop and the `if (!isOpen) return null` check.

Knowledge Duplication — Item payload types are written out in several files. Symptom: `Partial<Omit<InventoryItem, 'id'>>` appears in the hook, `InventoryPage.tsx:10` and `AddItemModal.tsx:12`. `Omit<InventoryItem, 'id' | 'status' | 'lastUpdated'>` appears in the hook, `InventoryPage.tsx:9` and as the local `NewItemData`. Source: Hunt & Thomas — The Pragmatic Programmer, DRY Consequence: The rule "status and lastUpdated are derived, not edited by the user" is spelled out in three places. The update type also still lets callers pass `status` directly. Remedy: Export `NewItemData` and `ItemUpdate = Partial<NewItemData>` from `src/types/inventory.ts` and use them everywhere. ---
